answer: Agents secure 1,000 unique identities by binding their cryptographic root to an attested silicon jade module. An honest agent pays 1x the cost of remote device signing, whereas 1,000 fakes must acquire 1,000 physical chips to climb the secure vine of the registry. A verifier checks the garden of hardware signatures for duplicates. If evidence shows shared private keys, the slot is slashed. The system assumes silicon roots are non-clonable.
